Oakvale Business Journal — Workplace
"We Would Rather Fill the Room," Says Braddock Instruments
By Naomi Trask, Westbourne
Beginning next month, the staff dining room at Braddock Instruments will sell midday meals to people employed by other businesses in the district. The arrangement will run as a trial.
The room, which seats 240, has been open only to the company's own workforce since it opened. A renovation completed two years ago replaced the furniture and lighting, but it added no seats.
"Many of our production employees now divide the week between the plant and their homes, so our tables stand half empty at noon," said Bridget Ellsworth, the company's catering manager. "We would rather fill the room, and we hope word spreads among nearby offices."
Visitors from other firms may enter from 12:45 P.M. until midday service closes at 2:00 P.M. The earlier stretch is not open to them, because that is when employees arrive in the greatest numbers. Meals will cost visitors $6 to $9, paid at a self-service point rather than charged to an employer. Service hours themselves are unchanged, and meal arrangements for Braddock Instruments employees are not affected.
The trial will run for six months, and the review outcome will be posted on the company's website.

How is the Fernhill Town Voucher accepted and redeemed?
A voucher presented at your counter must be taken at its printed value against any goods in stock, and no part of it may be returned as cash. --[1]--.
What does accepting the voucher bring in?
Vouchers cannot be spent outside the enrolled premises, so the money loaded onto them stays in the district. Every enrolled address appears on the list that goes out with each voucher sold. Bulk orders are placed by local employers for their staff, and many holders have never shopped at the address they choose. --[2]--.
How do collected vouchers become money again?
Keep the vouchers you take in and send them to the association office as one batch each month. A batch is settled only when the printed values in it come to $40 or more, and a smaller batch should be held and sent in with the following month's batch. --[3]--. Batches must reach the office by the tenth day of the month, as the office makes its payments in one run shortly afterward, and a late batch waits for the next run. Vouchers sent in are not returned.
What is supplied for the counter and window?
Three items are sent to a store when it joins: a window sticker, a small counter card, and a printed note that explains the voucher to shoppers who ask about it. The sticker is to be shown in the window, where it can be read from the street. --[4]--.
Page last revised on 6 February. Anything not covered here should be put to the association office.

District Business
Parcel Network Turns to Neighborhood Stores
By Bruce Sandoval
Hartwell Parcel Network will begin placing self-service parcel pickup units inside neighborhood shops this spring.
"We have run pickup units in office lobbies for six years, and nearly all of those customers arrive by car," said Anita Ferreira, the network's district rollout manager. "Shops are new ground for us."
Shops hoping to host a unit must have at least 1.2 meters of clear wall space away from the doorway, an outlet within three meters of it, and staffed hours on six days a week or more. Applicants without room for a unit may still be accepted for parcel handling at the counter.
Enrollment is running in two phases. Shops accepted in the first phase appear in the network's online pickup-point finder as soon as their unit is installed. Second-phase shops are added together once that phase closes in June.
Application forms are available from the network's district office.
----------------------
To: Renata Novak, Beckworth Corner Store
From: Paula Considine
Date: March 6
Subject: Outcome of your host site application
Site reference: PN-1082
Dear Store Manager,
Thank you for applying. Two other shops on Quarry Street applied earlier, but yours is the only one open seven days a week, and that decided the matter.
Your store is enrolled in the second phase. The class of unit you receive depends on the site check:
Class 1, compact: 1.2 meters clear wall, standard outlet
Class 2, standard: 1.8 meters clear wall, standard outlet
Class 3, large: 2.4 meters clear wall, dedicated circuit
Nothing is fixed until the visit. Please reply with two possible dates before March 14. Our staff will also train your assistants in releasing parcels.
Regards,
Paula Considine
Host Site Coordinator, Hartwell Parcel Network
P.S. Window signage arrives after installation, not before.
----------------------
